requirement: For each project source location Habeas supplies, the address MUST consist of the project-relative file and outline selector under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. This applies to the source metadata in mandatory inputs, acknowledgments, site matches and citation reviews, and to locations in Habeas tool diagnostics. These addresses MUST omit line and column coordinates. Quoted source retains its text, and an argument error may quote the agent's input.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers`. I did not request implementation source. I judged the tests against the requirement text and the supplied test bodies.

**Addresses are a project-relative file plus an outline selector**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` asserts the exact mandatory-input JSON for an anchored file. It contains `file: "skills/ready.md"`, `item: ""`, a hash, a kind and the quoted text, and no line or column keys.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` asserts `file == "src/lib.rs"` and `item == "fn[helper]"` in the mandatory inputs and in the review record. It also asserts that the root node is shown as `<root>` and that the prompt reads `Item under review: src/lib.rs fn[helper]`.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` asserts the site file and selector in the subject message, in the matches payload (`{kind, query, item}`) and in the record. It also asserts the `fixmes` item selector.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` asserts that a read result carries `file == "src/lib.rs"` and `selector == "fn[ready]"`.

**Mandatory inputs, acknowledgments, site matches and citation reviews omit line and column coordinates**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[subjects_of_one_kind_share_a_byte_identical_system_prompt]` covers requirement, example, structural, citation and site subjects. For each subject it checks every mandatory input and every model acknowledgment. Metadata, with `text` and `body` removed, must not match a position regex covering `.rs:N`, `line N` and the line/column keys. It also checks that `file` and `item` are strings and that the system prompt and subject message contain no positions.
- `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[sites_are_the_innermost_nodes_of_site_matches_and_violations_within_them]` asserts that `matches_value()` is exactly `{kind, query, item, text}`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[optional_requirement_and_example_reads_preserve_the_complete_declarations]` asserts that tool read results have no `line`, `line_start` or `line_end`.
- `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_discovery_returns_readable_nodes_without_recording_their_contents]` checks every lookup and named-query entry against the position regex. It asserts that each entry has only `node` and `data`, and that `source_address(...).selector` is a selector.

**Locations in tool diagnostics omit coordinates**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error]` covers several diagnostic forms:
  - a parse error with `line N`;
  - `file:N:` prefixes;
  - a second location inside one message (`first declared at md/a.md:3`);
  - a YAML `line X, column Y`;
  - a TOML `line, column`.
  
  It also asserts that numbers the model supplied itself, in the `src/lib.rs:9` and `src/lib.rs:3-9` forms, are kept.
- `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[named_query_errors_identify_the_source_without_exposing_a_line_number]` asserts that the named-query error contains `md/requirements.md#` and the reason, and has no cited line.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[source_tool_results_use_selectors_and_keep_locations_inside_quoted_code]` runs `read_node`, `outline_source`, `search_text` and `search_structure` through the CLI. It also runs a missing selector and an invalid selector. Every result must contain the `fn[kept]` selector, and the non-quoted parts must match no position regex. Missing and invalid selector errors show `quoted.rs#fn[`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` asserts that the excluded-read, missing-file and malformed-node errors contain no `line 1` or `:1:`.
- `src/authoring/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_rejects_excluded_and_unreadable_sources_without_domain_reads]` asserts that an invalid Rust file still yields an outline. The `read_node`, `search_structure` and outline payloads give the `file` and `selector` and match no position regex.
- `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[the_tool_reads_issues_with_the_token_and_redacts_bodies]` is marked for this requirement, but it is only tangentially relevant.

**Quoted source keeps its text, and an argument error may quote the agent's input**
- `source_tool_results_use_selectors_and_keep_locations_inside_quoted_code` asserts that the quoted `src/lib.rs:123` survives in the read text and in the search excerpts. The position check is applied only after the quote is removed.
- The `src/lib.rs:9` and `src/lib.rs:3-9` argument-error cases are preserved in `tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error`.

Every obligation has a test that asserts its outcome. The relevant tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject, and I found no marking gap. The requirement it cites, `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, is context only, so I did not reassess its grammar here.
